subject: Biology
question: Hibernation in animals is an adaptation that primarily helps them
options: survive periods of cold and food scarcity

increase their metabolic rate Correct Answer: B Explanation: Hibernation is a state of dormancy during winter/cold periods when food is scarce. Animals reduce metabolic rate, body temperature, and energy consumption to survive unfavourable conditions. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Hibernation is metabolic dormancy, not predator escape. C. Migration is a separate strategy involving movement; hibernation is staying put in dormancy. D. During hibernation, metabolic rate is drastically reduced, not increased.

subject: Biology
question: The mouthpart adaptation of the butterfly for feeding on nectar is a
options: coiled siphoning proboscis Correct Answer: D Explanation: Butterflies have a long, coiled proboscis (siphoning type) which they uncoil to reach nectar deep within flowers. It operates like a drinking straw. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Biting/chewing mandibles are found in cockroaches and grasshoppers. B. Piercing/sucking mouthparts are found in mosquitoes. C. The housefly uses a sponging labellum.

subject: Biology
question: Aestivation in animals like lungfish is an adaptation to
options: hot and dry conditions with water shortage

deep-sea pressure Correct Answer: B Explanation: Aestivation is a summer dormancy in response to heat and drought. Lungfish burrow into mud and secrete a mucus cocoon when water bodies dry up, entering dormancy until the rains return. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Dormancy in cold is hibernation. C. High altitude adaptation involves physiological changes (more red blood cells), not dormancy. D. Deep-sea organisms have pressure adaptations but not aestivation.

subject: Biology
question: The warning colouration of mushrooms serves to
options: camouflage the mushroom in its forest environment

reflect sunlight to aid photosynthesis Correct Answer: B Explanation: Aposematic (warning) colouration uses bright or conspicuous colours to advertise unpalatability or toxicity to potential predators — a form of chemical defence signalling. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Mushrooms do not need insect pollination — they disperse by spores. C. Warning colouration does the opposite of camouflage. D. Mushrooms are fungi and do not photosynthesize.

subject: Biology
question: Male Agama lizards display bright red-head colouration primarily to
options: camouflage themselves from predators Correct Answer: C Explanation: The red coloration of the male Agama lizard head is a sexual selection characteristic — it attracts females and signals dominance to rival males during the breeding season. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Agama lizards are not toxic; the colour is for sexual selection. B. Thermoregulation occurs through basking behaviour, not colouration. D. Bright red is conspicuous — the opposite of camouflage.

subject: Biology
question: A stick insect's resemblance to a twig is an example of
options: countershading Correct Answer: C Explanation: Camouflage or cryptic colouration is when an organism blends with its environment to avoid detection. The stick insect's twig-like shape and brown/green colour make it nearly invisible among branches. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Warning colouration (aposematism) uses bright conspicuous colours. B. Mimicry is when a harmless species resembles a harmful or unpalatable one. D. Countershading is a specific pattern of dark above, light below.

subject: Biology
question: Which feature is characteristic of mammals that distinguishes them from all other vertebrates?
options: Presence of hair and mammary glands

Four-chambered heart Correct Answer: B Explanation: The defining features of Class Mammalia are the presence of hair (or fur) on the body and mammary glands that produce milk to nourish young. These are unique to mammals. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Birds are also warm-blooded (endothermic). C. Internal fertilization also occurs in reptiles and birds. D. Birds also have a four-chambered heart.

subject: Biology
question: Spirogyra is classified as a Thallophyte because it
options: is found only in marine environments Correct Answer: A Explanation: Thallophytes have an undifferentiated plant body called a thallus — they lack true roots, stems, and leaves. Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga with no such differentiated structures. Why the other options are wrong: • B. Thallophytes lack vascular tissue. C. Spirogyra can reproduce sexually by conjugation. D. Spirogyra is a freshwater alga.

subject: Biology
question: The main difference between monocots and dicots is that monocots have
options: one cotyledon, parallel leaf venation, and fibrous roots

woody stems and broad leaves Correct Answer: C Explanation: Monocotyledons (e.g. maize, grasses) have one seed leaf (cotyledon), leaves with parallel venation, fibrous root systems, and floral parts in multiples of three. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Two cotyledons define dicots. B. Net/reticulate venation and taproot systems are dicot features. D. Woody stems are more associated with dicot trees.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following organisms reproduces by binary fission?
options: Yeast Correct Answer: B Explanation: Paramecium (a protozoan) reproduces asexually by binary fission — splitting into two identical daughter cells. This is the primary mode of asexual reproduction in most unicellular organisms. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Rhizopus (a fungus) reproduces by spore formation. C. Hydra reproduces asexually by budding. D. Yeast reproduces asexually by budding.

subject: Biology
question: The life cycle of a butterfly includes the stages: egg → larva → pupa → adult. This type of metamorphosis is called
options: ametabolous development Correct Answer: B Explanation: Complete metamorphosis (holometabolism) involves four distinct stages: egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa (chrysalis), and adult. Butterflies undergo this type of development. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Incomplete metamorphosis (e.g. cockroach) has three stages: egg → nymph → adult, with no pupal stage. C. 'Simple metamorphosis' is another name for incomplete metamorphosis. D. Ametabolous development (no metamorphosis) occurs in silverfish.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following best describes the structural complexity of animals from coelenterates to mammals?
options: Tissue → cellular → organ system → organ Correct Answer: C Explanation: The evolutionary progression in animal complexity goes from the cellular level (coelenterates/sponges) → tissue level (flatworms) → organ level → organ system level (vertebrates including mammals). Why the other options are wrong: • A. This incorrectly places 'organ system' before 'organ'. B. This starts with organ — incorrect. D. This places tissue before cell — incorrect.

subject: Biology
question: Earthworms belong to the phylum Annelida. Their most distinctive feature is
options: a pseudocoelom Correct Answer: C Explanation: Annelids are defined by their segmented (annulated) body plan. Earthworms have tiny bristles called setae on each segment which aid in locomotion. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Jointed appendages define Arthropoda. B. A mantle and shell define Mollusca. D. Earthworms are true coelomates; pseudocoelom is found in nematodes.

subject: Biology
question: Rhizopus is used as an example of Fungi because it
options: has a thallus body with chlorophyll
is multicellular, lacks chlorophyll, and reproduces by spores

is prokaryotic with peptidoglycan walls Correct Answer: C Explanation: Rhizopus (bread mould) is a fungus — it is multicellular (filamentous hyphae), heterotrophic (saprophytic), lacks chlorophyll, and reproduces by producing spores in sporangia. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Rhizopus is multicellular and non-photosynthetic. B. Fungi lack chlorophyll and do not have a thallus body in the algal sense. D. Fungi are eukaryotic and have chitin walls, not peptidoglycan.

subject: Biology
question: The gradual transition of plants from aquatic to terrestrial life can be traced through
options: Bryophyta → Thallophyta → Pteridophyta → Gymnospermae Correct Answer: B Explanation: The evolutionary progression from aquatic to terrestrial life in plants follows: Thallophyta (fully aquatic, e.g. Spirogyra) → Bryophyta (moist terrestrial, still need water for fertilisation) → Pteridophyta (vascular, more independent) → Spermatophyta (seed plants, fully independent of water for reproduction). Why the other options are wrong: • A. This describes kingdom evolution, not plant terrestrial adaptation. C. This is in reverse order. D. This incorrectly places Thallophyta after Bryophyta. SECTION B: FORM AND FUNCTIONS

subject: Biology
question: The vascular bundle arrangement that is scattered throughout the cross-section of the stem is characteristic of
options: ferns Correct Answer: B Explanation: In monocot stems (e.g. maize), vascular bundles are scattered randomly throughout the ground tissue. In dicot stems, they are arranged in a ring (circle). Why the other options are wrong: • A. Dicot stems have vascular bundles arranged in a ring. C. Gymnosperms have vascular bundles in a ring like dicots. D. Ferns have their own vascular arrangement but bundles are not scattered as in monocots.

subject: Biology
question: The tissue responsible for the lateral growth (increase in girth) of a dicotyledonous stem is the
options: epidermis Correct Answer: C Explanation: The vascular cambium is a meristematic tissue that produces new xylem (secondary xylem, wood) and phloem cells, resulting in secondary growth and increase in stem girth. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Collenchyma provides flexible support but does not produce new cells for growth. B. Sclerenchyma provides rigid support. D. Epidermis is a protective tissue.

subject: Biology
question: In a leaf, the palisade mesophyll is adapted for photosynthesis because it
options: is located below the spongy mesophyll and has fewer chloroplasts
is located near the upper epidermis and contains densely packed cells with many chloroplasts
contains large air spaces for gaseous exchange

has a waxy cuticle that prevents water loss Correct Answer: B Explanation: Palisade mesophyll cells are column-shaped, densely packed, and rich in chloroplasts. They are positioned just below the upper epidermis to maximise light absorption for photosynthesis. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Palisade is near the upper surface and has MORE chloroplasts. C. Large air spaces are found in the spongy mesophyll, which is adapted for gas exchange. D. The waxy cuticle is on the epidermis.

subject: Biology
question: The function of xylem vessels in a flowering plant is to
options: transport organic solutes from leaves to all parts of the plant
transport water and mineral salts from roots to leaves
provide flexible support to the plant

store starch in the root cortex Correct Answer: B Explanation: Xylem is responsible for the upward transport of water and dissolved mineral salts from the roots to the rest of the plant (transpiration stream). It is a one-way transport system. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Transport of organic solutes (sugars) is the function of phloem. C. Flexible support is provided by collenchyma. D. Starch storage in root cortex is a function of parenchyma cells.

subject: Biology
question: The mammalian kidney is located in the
options: cranial cavity Correct Answer: C Explanation: The kidneys are paired organs located in the posterior abdominal cavity, lying behind the peritoneum (retroperitoneal) on either side of the vertebral column. Why the other options are wrong: • A. The thoracic cavity contains the lungs and heart. B. The pericardial cavity surrounds the heart. D. The cranial cavity contains the brain.

subject: Biology
question: The dark reaction of photosynthesis (Calvin cycle) occurs in the
options: cytoplasm of the cell Correct Answer: B Explanation: The light-independent (dark) reactions occur in the stroma — the fluid-filled region of the chloroplast surrounding the thylakoids. CO2 is fixed here in the Calvin cycle using ATP and NADPH from the light reactions. Why the other options are wrong: • A. The grana (stacks of thylakoids) are where the light-dependent reactions occur. C. The outer membrane is just the envelope; no reactions occur there. D. The Calvin cycle is confined to the chloroplast stroma.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is a product of the light-dependent reaction of photosynthesis?
options: RuBP and G3P Correct Answer: B Explanation: During the light-dependent stage, light energy splits water (photolysis), releasing O2. The energy is used to produce ATP and NADPH (reduced NADP), which power the Calvin cycle. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Glucose is produced in the dark reaction (Calvin cycle). C. Starch is a storage form of glucose produced later; water is a reactant not product here. D. RuBP and G3P are intermediates of the Calvin cycle (dark reactions).

subject: Biology
question: A plant growing in nitrogen-deficient soil is most likely to show
options: yellowing of older leaves (chlorosis) due to reduced chlorophyll synthesis
wilting of stems due to loss of turgor

early flowering Correct Answer: B Explanation: Nitrogen is essential for protein and chlorophyll synthesis. Nitrogen deficiency leads to chlorosis (yellowing) starting in older leaves, as nitrogen is mobilised from them to support new growth. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Purple discolouration from anthocyanin accumulation is often associated with phosphorus deficiency. C. Wilting is caused by water deficit, not nitrogen deficiency. D. Nitrogen deficiency typically stunts growth; early flowering is not a typical symptom.

subject: Biology
question: The food test for the presence of reducing sugars uses
options: Ethanol (turns milky white) Correct Answer: C Explanation: Benedict's test detects reducing sugars. When heated with Benedict's solution (blue), a positive result gives an orange-red/brick-red precipitate due to the reduction of copper(II) ions to copper(I) oxide. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Biuret reagent tests for proteins (turns purple). B. Iodine tests for starch (turns blue-black). D. The ethanol emulsion test detects lipids/fats (turns milky white when water is added).

subject: Biology
question: Which deficiency disease is caused by insufficient vitamin C in the diet?
options: Scurvy Correct Answer: D Explanation: Scurvy is caused by vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency. Vitamin C is needed for collagen synthesis; deficiency causes bleeding gums, loose teeth, bruising, and poor wound healing. Why the other options are wrong: • A. Rickets is caused by vitamin D / calcium / phosphorus deficiency. B. Kwashiorkor is caused by protein deficiency. C. Pellagra is caused by niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency.
